review: 1:1 יְהֹוָה יֵשׁוּעַ — the Arabic itself prints يَهْوَه يَسُوعُ رَبَّنَا, applying the divine name to Jesus; the Hebrew keeps the tetragrammaton exactly as the Arabic has it rather than substituting אֲדֹנָי, because the hymn's whole argument is that this is who was before the mountains.

1:2–1:4 — the stanza is Psalm 90:2 (בְּטֶרֶם הָרִים יֻלָּדוּ … וַתְּהִי אֶרֶץ וְתֵבֵל) crossed with Proverbs 8:25–30 (בְּטֶרֶם הָרִים הָטְבָּעוּ … וָאֶהְיֶה שַׁעֲשׁוּעִים); the Arabic قَبْلَ الْجِبَال … قَبْلَ تَكَوُّنِ التِّلَال is those verses.
2:1 שַׁעֲשׁוּעַ — Proverbs 8:30 (וָאֶהְיֶה שַׁעֲשׁוּעִים יוֹם יוֹם); the Arabic لَذَّةً is 'delight', and שַׁעֲשׁוּעַ is the word the Wisdom text uses of the Son's eternal delight.
2:3 בְּאֵין תְּהֹמוֹת — Proverbs 8:24 (בְּאֵין תְּהֹמוֹת חוֹלָלְתִּי); the Arabic إِذْ لَمْ يَكُنْ غَمْرٌ quotes that line, and Hebrew keeps תְּהוֹמוֹת.

3:4 חָדַלְתָּ עַד־קֵץ עַד — 'You did not cease to the very end of the age'; the Arabic وَلَمْ تَزَلْ إِلَى طُولِ الْمَدَى is 'You have not ceased through all duration', and the doubled עַד reproduces the Arabic's emphasis.
